header:
Date: 2026-07-08
Time: 10:00 AM PDT
Duration: 46 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Camila Ruiz (Redwood CSM), Priya Menon (Novena Head of Security), Ethan Shaw (Novena Platform), Lina Ortiz (Novena PM)
summary: Weekly pilot sync to review security/compliance results from week 2 of the Novena Medical pilot. Focus: SSO/SAML setup, audit logging options and retention, SOC2 evidence mapping, KMS/encryption, and next steps to satisfy Novena's compliance gate for production pilot expansion.
topics: Audit logs: schema, retention, export options
SOC2 control alignment and evidence collection
Short-term mitigations and timeline to compliance gate
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we've got about 45 minutes. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Priya Menon: Priya here.
[00:10] Ethan Shaw: Ethan on the line.
[00:12] Lina Ortiz: Lina here.
[00:14] Marcus Lee: Marcus from Redwood. Camila's here as well.
[00:16] Sofia Patel: Cool. Agenda — status on SSO, audit logs, SOC2 mapping, KMS questions, and then action items.
[00:30] Priya Menon: Quick update from our side, we did a preliminary review of the sandbox logs you shared, we saw token ids but not the full KV cache keys, which is fine, but we need to confirm what fields are persisted long-term.
[00:45] Marcus Lee: Right, so the sandbox uses a short retention window by default, and we scrub PII on ingest where configured. Note, the exported log sample we sent had some names anonymized, but the raw event includes request metadata — not user payload unless you enable retention.
[01:05] Ethan Shaw: When you say "scrub PII" — is that automatic or a policy we toggle? We need to know for our data protection officer.
[01:15] Marcus Lee: It's policy-driven. There are two levers: real-time redaction at the routing layer, and post-ingest retention filters. For the pilot we've got redaction off by default so you can validate model outputs; you can turn on redaction and then we won't persist certain fields. I should add, our KMS integration can also encrypt logs at rest with a customer-managed key.
[01:40] Priya Menon: Ok that matters. SOC2 will want to see key management and access controls. Do you provide an audit trail of key rotations?
[01:50] Camila Ruiz: We do provide rotation metadata — the control plane logs key rotations and who initiated them. We'll include an excerpt in the SOC2 mapping doc.
[02:05] Lina Ortiz: Marcus, quick technical Q — can we push audit logs to our S3 bucket in addition to Redwood's console export?
[02:15] Marcus Lee: Yes, you can configure log sinks. We support pushing structured JSON events to a pre-auth'd S3 or to your SIEM via our event forwarder. There's a small latency — typically under a minute — and we batch writes for efficiency.
[02:35] Priya Menon: Great. One thing flagged in our review: retention policies. We need two-tier retention — 30 days full detail, and 365 days aggregated metrics. Is that supported?
[02:50] Marcus Lee: Yes, that's a common pattern. We can keep full events for 30 days and then rollup to metrics-only for a year. That rollup loses PII and request-level text, but still preserves counters and anomaly signals.
[03:10] Ethan Shaw: How is the rollup performed? Is it irreversible?
[03:15] Marcus Lee: The rollup is irreversible by design — it's part of retention compliance. We can snapshot the raw logs if you need for a forensics window before roll-up, but that increases storage and cost.
[03:35] Priya Menon: Cost tradeoffs are fine if we get the compliance guarantees. Also SSO — we started SAML setup; we hit a cert mismatch when importing your metadata.
[03:45] Sofia Patel: Marcus, can you take us through the usual idP exchange flow and where cert issues crop up?
[03:52] Marcus Lee: Sure. Commonly the issue is the base64 cert block in the metadata having line breaks or an extra header — some IdPs export metadata with a different encoding. We'll accept metadata upload or manual entry of the EntityID and certificate. We also support IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows.
[04:20] Ethan Shaw: We prefer SP-initiated. Also need SCIM for groups to map RBAC. Do you support SCIM provisioning?
[04:28] Camila Ruiz: Yes, we support SCIM v2 for group/user provisioning. We can sync groups into Redwood RBAC and map to roles like admin, developer, auditor.
[04:40] Priya Menon: Perfect. For SOC2 evidence, we'll need an export of admin role changes for the pilot period. Is that in the audit log?
[04:48] Marcus Lee: Yes, admin-level changes are logged with actor, timestamp, and the before/after state. We can produce CSV or JSON exports.
[05:02] Lina Ortiz: On the functional side, we ran two inference workloads this week — latency and quality checks. Quick numbers: average generation latency at p50 was 210ms on your hosted API profile you recommended, p95 was 680ms.
[05:20] Marcus Lee: Those numbers sound consistent with a hosted small model profile. Did you run with KV cache warm?
[05:25] Lina Ortiz: Warm for the second run, cold first run. We saw costs roughly linearly follow token usage.
[05:35] Sofia Patel: Good data point. For compliance gate, Priya — what are the must-have items to move to the next phase?
[05:42] Priya Menon: Must-haves: SAML SSO in production with SCIM for groups, audit-log export to our S3 decoupled from Redwood console, SOC2 control mapping and attestations for key controls, and demonstration of retention enforcement (actual deletion/rollup). Also want KMS with customer-managed keys for any persisted sensitive artifacts.
[06:05] Marcus Lee: Understood. For KMS, we support external KMS via standard AWS KMS grants or via HSM integrations for on-prem. If you're using our Private deployment we can also support HSM in VPC.
[06:20] Ethan Shaw: We're planning a Private deployment if the pilot meets compliance, can you outline the differences for logs and key management?
[06:27] Marcus Lee: In Private you control the network and can host the log sink inside your VPC. Log ingress still passes through our runtime agents but storage stays in your account — that enables full isolation and your KMS. For hosted, logs are in Redwood's storage with export hooks.
[06:44] Priya Menon: SOC2 reviewers also ask about access reviews. Can you provide quarterly access review exports automatically?
[06:53] Camila Ruiz: We can schedule automated exports of IAM roles, active sessions, and access changes. We'll add that to the mapping doc.
[07:05] Lina Ortiz: Regarding PII redaction test — Marcus you mentioned runtime redaction. Can that be configured per route? We have different models that handle PHI vs general support chat.
[07:16] Marcus Lee: Yes, redaction is route-configurable. You can set a routing policy where requests to the PHI model route through redaction enabled paths and also pinned to Private or Dedicated capacity.
[07:30] Priya Menon: We saw a couple of misattributed speakers in the transcript sample — minor, but point being we need fidelity in logs so audits are traceable to the right actor.
[07:40] Marcus Lee: Noted. Our agent includes request.client_id and user.assumed_identity if SSO is used. That maps back to your IdP subject. We'll show sample mappings.
[07:55] Sofia Patel: Quick question on retention enforcement demonstration — can Marcus set up a demo where we create a few synthetic events, then run the rollup and show the deletion?
[08:04] Marcus Lee: Yes, I can run that in the sandbox. I suggest doing it with a copy of your S3 sink so you can validate deletion on your side as well.
[08:15] Ethan Shaw: Also, can you show proof that backups are subject to the same policy?
[08:20] Marcus Lee: Backups follow the same lifecycle. We'll include the backup retention config in the export.
[08:30] Priya Menon: On encryption in flight — TLS is fine — but our auditors also want mutual TLS for the event forwarder. Do you support mTLS?
[08:39] Marcus Lee: Yes, our event forwarder supports mTLS with client cert validation. We'll include setup steps in the docs.
[08:48] Lina Ortiz: Switching briefly to SOC2 mapping — Camila, have you drafted the control mapping?
[08:53] Camila Ruiz: Yes, a draft. It maps Redwood controls to CC6.1, CC7.2, etc. I will attach the draft to the follow-up email. We'll also include the artifact list: config exports, admin change logs, KMS rotation records, and SAML metadata.
[09:12] Priya Menon: Excellent. One risk callout — we are evaluating AnthraCloud concurrently; their offering includes native SIEM streaming which they emphasize, but your rollup and Private options are compelling.
[09:25] Sofia Patel: Noted. Anything specific we should highlight to the auditors about how Redwood handles model fallbacks or graceful degradation?
[09:33] Marcus Lee: We have routing policies and automatic fallback to lower-cost model variants; all fallbacks are logged with reason codes. For compliance, we can restrict fallback in production so a critical route never falls back.
[09:47] Ethan Shaw: Does that mean we can set a policy: no fallback for PHI routes?
[09:50] Marcus Lee: Exactly. You can lock a route to a dedicated pool and disable fallback.
[09:58] Lina Ortiz: Ok, timeline recap please — we want to present to the audit committee next Friday 2026-07-17. Can we have SOC2 mapping and audit-log export sample before then?
[10:07] Camila Ruiz: We'll prioritize that. Sofia, Marcus — can you commit to the export by Friday 2026-07-10?
[10:13] Sofia Patel: Yes, we can get the export and SOC2 excerpt by 7/10. Marcus?
[10:16] Marcus Lee: Yes. I'll also run the retention demo in sandbox and share steps.
[10:20] Priya Menon: Great. A couple of quick clarifying Qs — about pricing: dedicated capacity for PHI routes, will that be quoted separately?
[10:28] Sofia Patel: We'll send an updated pilot quote with dedicated pricing options and estimated monthly cost delta for the dedicated PHI pool.
[10:35] Ethan Shaw: For legal, we need a data processing addendum and an SOP for incident response. Can you provide templates?
[10:42] Camila Ruiz: Yes, we'll attach the DPA template and incident response playbook.
[10:47] Lina Ortiz: One last technical note: can we run a redaction benchmark to see latency impact? We expect some overhead.
[10:53] Marcus Lee: Absolutely, I can run that in parallel with the retention demo. We'll include before/after p50/p95 and CPU profiles.
[11:04] Sofia Patel: Ok let's recap action items and owners — and then we'll close.
[11:10] Priya Menon: Thanks all.
[11:12] Sofia Patel: Thanks everyone, we will follow up with the docs and schedule the demo week of 7/13.
[11:18] End of recording
